notes: This descriptor documents the currently active packaged PRoot asset.
Active runtime is the KF lifecycle telemetry build from the Termux PRoot fork.
PRoot emits low-cost fork/clone/vfork/exec/exit/signal JSONL events to KF_PROOT_TELEMETRY_PATH.

Lifecycle v3 additionally exports telemetrySessionId, prootStartMs, processGroupId, sessionId, exitCode, signal, and scans the full exec envp for whitelisted KF_RUNTIME_ID/KF_UNIT_ID values when present.
Lifecycle v4 additionally projects high-value /proc/<pid> files through KF_PROCFS_PROJECTION_ROOT so Ubuntu process queries can consume PRoot event-backed facts without broad rescans.

Lifecycle v5 additionally keeps inherited command/runtime identity on fork/clone/vfork events and preserves last command identity on exit/signal events; runtime-process-table.tsv exposes started_at_ms.
Lifecycle v6 additionally rotates the raw telemetry JSONL at 8 MiB with three archives; KF retains all running tracees and bounds terminal live-table history to 5000 entries or 7 days.
Lifecycle v7 keeps procfs projection for normal Ubuntu commands but lets kf-resource-sampler bypass stat/statm projection and update runtime-process-table resource columns.
Lifecycle v8 additionally lets standard resource-view commands such as ps aux and top bypass stat/statm projection while refreshing runtime-process-table resource columns on read.
Lifecycle v9 emits eventSeq, lifecycleSeq, parentLifecycleSeq, and startTimeTicks, and maintains a per-PRoot active tracee registry for cold-start and event-gap reconciliation.
Lifecycle v10 fixes active-registry JSON framing so native registry snapshots can be parsed during cold-start and event-gap reconciliation.
Lifecycle v11 retries identity capture for the initial tracee at its first event, preventing owner shutdown from falling back to shared Android process groups.
Lifecycle v12 atomically retires empty active-registry sessions, keeping registry cost proportional to current live PRoot sessions instead of accumulated history.

Lifecycle v13 adds a write-before resource transaction journal behind KF_PROOT_TXN_CONTROL_PATH, serializes cross-PRoot captures, enforces the configured backup budget, and receives pre-mutation notifications for link2symlink host-side rewrites.
Lifecycle v14 canonicalizes mutation paths before hashing and capture so aliases such as user-home and user-home/. share one first-write preimage.
Lifecycle v15 applies POSIX root clamping to absolute paths containing leading parent segments so outside-root mutations remain transparent instead of aborting the tracee.
Lifecycle v16 skips preimage capture for creation syscalls whose destination already exists, preventing idempotent mkdir and link helpers from snapshotting unchanged directory trees.

Lifecycle v17 generalizes the control and journal wire format to protected file operations, keeps legacy resource transaction wire compatibility, and adds 64 KiB range undo capture for direct writes, vectored writes, sendfile, splice, copy_file_range, and truncate.

Lifecycle v17 escalates destructive path changes, metadata changes, fallocate, and shared mmap to a whole-object fallback; range rollback overlays the older blocks on that fallback to reconstruct the exact pre-operation file.

Lifecycle v18 adds the PRoot View filesystem projection: immutable Base, writable Upper, whiteout deletion, linear parent layers, shared cross-process generation, and repeatable scope_root boundaries.
Lifecycle v18 protects the container rootfs plus managed workspace software and bin scopes while leaving other workspace paths directly persistent.
Lifecycle v19 lets a create operation replace a path hidden by a whiteout, covering unlink-then-install update tools without exposing the immutable Base.
Lifecycle v20 replaces regular-file whole copy-up with 64 KiB sparse block deltas and checksummed double-slot metadata while keeping Base immutable.
Lifecycle v20 preserves parent View chains, fd identity, shared mmap visibility, ARM32 large-file ABI, and fails closed for destructive syscalls that are not safely virtualized.
Lifecycle v21 keeps ordinary View processes on the existing PRoot seccomp fast path and installs fd plus mmap lifecycle filters only after a block-backed file is opened.
Lifecycle v22 collapses descendant whiteouts into one ancestor marker when recursively deleting a lower directory, allowing rm -rf and same-path recreation without touching Base.

Lifecycle v23 normalizes canonical host paths before View lookup, so directory-walking tools such as mkdir -p can enter a directory created in Upper and continue creating nested children without falling back to Base.
PRoot is a fact source only; Android/KF remains the policy and execution authority.
Stock PRoot remains packaged as a no-telemetry fallback.
Legacy termux-baseline remains packaged only as quarantined historical metadata.
Runtime migration preserves containers, shared workspace, containers.json, and terminal-sessions.json while rewriting APK-owned runtime assets.
